summary: Voice AI platform for expressive speech, cloning, transcription, and real-time APIs.
editor_note: Voice models are becoming application infrastructure, but most demos optimize for a perfect sentence. Fish Audio makes a different bet: emotional control and consistency across five minutes matter more than a five-second clone. Its surface exposes text-to-speech, cloning, transcription, emotion tags, real-time APIs, and a 2 million-voice library. Unlike an enterprise API, it offers open models and self-hosting. The risk is whether consent and rights controls scale with user-uploaded voices.
tags: voice ai,text to speech,voice cloning,speech api,open source

product_evidence.claim: Fish Audio exposes expressive text-to-speech, voice cloning, speech-to-text, emotion controls, and real-time APIs alongside a public library of more than 2 million voices.
Developers can use hosted APIs or open and self-hosted models, while the funding announcement reports support for more than 83 languages and word-level emotion control.

market_context.primary_user: Developers, creators, and enterprises building expressive speech, voice-agent, localization, and audio-generation products.
market_context.differentiation: Fish Audio combines controllable expressive speech, cloning, open models, self-hosting, and hosted real-time APIs on one public developer surface.
market_context.why_now: Voice is becoming a common interface for agents and media workflows, increasing demand for low-latency multilingual speech with controllable emotion.

risks.claim: The falsifiable risk is whether consent, provenance, removal, and rights controls keep pace as a user-uploaded library grows beyond 2 million voices.
risks.basis: VentureDex editorial assessment based on the official public library, developer surface, and funding announcement.
